profile_text.body:
iNaturalist is a social network for naturalists, according to its own site. The company describes it as a place to record observations of plants and animals, share them with friends and researchers, and learn about the natural world. Users open the app and photograph any wild plant, animal, fungi, or other organism, from their neighborhood or anywhere in the world. The site says observations are open and freely available to researchers, conservation practitioners, and curious individuals, and that when the community agrees on an identification, an observation becomes "research grade" and enters the global scientific record. It is available on the web at iNaturalist.org and through mobile apps.

The tracked product is iNaturalist, listed under Education and Research AI. Its AI feature is species suggestions. The stated audience is students 13 and older and teachers, with students younger than 13 allowed with parent permission. The note describes consumer terms with no school agreement, most content public by default, and a parental permission process for users 12 and under. It is free.

The site highlights examples of the community's role in discovery and conservation, including the Frosted Phoenix moth, spotted in New Zealand after decades without a sighting and once thought extinct, and Inimia nat, abbreviated I. nat, a new-to-science mantis species found by a woman in Australia walking in her neighborhood. It also describes local volunteers in California who came together through iNaturalist to protect migrating amphibians crossing a busy road. The site presents the platform as a resource for research on understudied taxa and as a way to contribute to conserving natural heritage.
